policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'the Chaldeans' permits both the qere and ketiv spellings and no mapped textual-variant note distinguishes them; retain the qere base fallback.
ASV 'she doted upon them' permits both verbal forms; the Hebrew gloss 'at the sight of her eyes' does not distinguish the qere from the ketiv, so retain the qere base fallback.
ASV explicitly renders 'drunkards,' distinguishing the ketiv סובאים from the qere סָבָאִים.
ASV explicitly has 'Now,' distinguishing the qere עַתָּה from ketiv עת; the mapped notes are alternative renderings or a Hebrew gloss, not textual variants.
ASV's main wording 'will they play the harlot' is plural and therefore distinguishes qere יִזְנוּ from singular ketiv יזנה; the alternative-rendering notes do not decide a reading.
